div.p: In this paper, we propose a multimedia server scheduling technique to efficiently integrate hard realtime and multimedia soft real-time tasks in the same system. For two different classes, we show how to adjust the fraction of the CPU bandwidth assigned to each task using the adaptable scheduling where each task instance is split proportionally into the server. The proposed method is capable of minimizing the mean tardiness of multimedia tasks, without jeopardizing the schedulability of the hard tasks. The performance of this scheduling method is compared with that of similar mechanisms through simulation experiments.

div.head: Introduction
div.p: Many hard real-time applications such as automated manufacturing md attack helicopters are being designed to take advantage of audio and video information [']. This information needs real-time support because of the sensitivity to delay and jitter tolerance [']. In particular, support for processing video information must co-exist with that for the hard reakime control information in distributed real-time industrial control applications Accommodating multimedia soft and traditional hard real-time applications that have interaction requirements is a challenging research issue. In recent years, there has been an abundance of research in the area of scheduling algorithms". "I.

In general, they are based on a conventional reakime scheduler such as EDF(Ear1iest Deadline First) or RM(Rate Monotonic). In';, 41, a scheduling methodology is proposed to reserve a fraction of the processor bandwidth to each task. To efficiently handle the problem of task overloads, each task is scheduled by a dedicated server, which does not require the knowledge of the WCET( Worst Case Execution Time) and assigns a suitable deadline to the served task whenever the reserved time is consumed. Periodic tasks do not, however, have special treatment in this scheduling scheme.

In this paper, we discuss how to provide efficient runtime support to mu1timedi.a applications in a real-time system, where two types of tasks can coexist simultaneously: multimedia soft real-time periodic tasks and hard real-time periodic: tasks. Hard tasks are guaranteed based on WCET, whereas multimedia soft tasks are served based on mean parameters. In multimedia applications, soft deadline misses may decrease the QoS, but do not cause critical system faults. Therefore, treating multimedia tasks as hard real-time tasks is not appropriate, firstly because an underestimation of the WCET would compromise the guarantee done on the other tasks. Secondly, it would be very inefficient, since trying to guarantee a task with a WCET much greater than its mean execution time would cause a waste of the CPU resource. This problem can be solved hy a bandwidth reservation strategy, which assigns each soft. task a maximum bandwidth, calculated using the mean execution time.

To provide good guarantees to multimedia tasks, the proposed scheduling algorithm integrates hard real-time and multimedia tasks using a variable bandwidth server with the minimum period. The primary goal of our research is to minimize the mean time that soft tasks execute after their deadlines while guaranteeing all the hard tasks. For multimedia applications in a real-time system, this paper presents a performance evaluation that provides better performance for handling two types of tasks in the same system.

div.head: Preemption policy
div.p: Hard real-time tasks and multimedia tasks are scheduled based on the EDF scheduler, respectively. It is, however, assumed that hard real-time tasks have higher priority over multiiiiedia tasks in this paper. With the help of preemption policy, the timing constraint of the hard real-time task is never sacrificed in this scheduling procedure . ,

div.head: Experimental Results
div.p: In this section we compare the VBS(Variab1e Bandwidth Server) with other similar service mechanism, namely the Constant Bandwidth Ser~er(CBS)[~l. The main difference between VBS and CBS is visible when the actual computation time of the inultiinedia task is larger than its mean execution. In fact, while the CBS delays this multimedia task until the next budget (that occurs at the next server), the VBS tries to execute it within the budget of multimedia tasks without jeopardizing the schedulability of the hard real-time tasks. This difference in scheduling multimedia tasks, causes a big difference in the performance offered by the 1wo servers to soft realtime tasks. div.head: Conclusion
div.p: In this paper, we presented the variable bandwidth server to integrate hard real-time and multimedia soft real-time computing in a single system, under the EDF scheduling algorithm. The objective of this server is i o minimize the mean tardiness of multimedia tasks, without jcopardizing thc schcdulability of thc hard rcal-timc tasks. The proposed server has been compared with other known server, obtaining higher CPU utilization. We showed through simulations that the tardiness experienced by soft tasks under the proposed server is much sinaller than that experienced using the CBS. This scheduling solution is also expected to support an adaptive QoS degradation or multimedia sessions durine system overload.
